_about: Components: the equipment a mech's die is made of. Each is exactly one entry on the die (its face: the engine's word for one entry). Nothing generic exists: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. A component a chassis lists under fixed is built in and is never bought or crafted, which is what makes it unique. Damage sits at the scale of fives, the rest at the scale of tens: magnitudes, not steps (any whole number; docs/rules.md). A rolled entry carries power and power_max and rolls between them; a flat entry is one number and involves no roll. There are no crits (10 October). Keywords are a list; authored entries should stay under the validator's cap, upgrades may push past it. passive is null or one object, same shape as a chassis passive. A face's kind makes it a weapon (attack: spent on a foe, need not deal damage) or equipment (shield, vent: spent on a machine); equipment may carry targets, self_ally (the default), self or ally, and the die shows a chip for a narrowed one. design.stage is draft until Ryan signs the entry off as final; nothing is final yet. Shown to the player: codex (the inspect entry), flavour (a quote); both still to be written. design is internal and never shown: fantasy, niche. Numbers are placeholders. A component the engine cannot run yet carries "status": "planned": it is kept, its face is checked for shape, a keyword the vocabulary names but the engine lacks is allowed on it, and the die builds it without that keyword. tier (7 October, bible section 10, the ledger): a component stocked by any chassis takes the lowest tier of the chassis that stock it, derived and never stored; one that no chassis stocks carries its own tier; a fixed-only component has none. Tier one is the blueprints a run starts with, and the capital's maker has no tier-one component. shape is the silhouette class the model wears when the component is fitted (decided 29 September, the rule settled 30 September: hardpoints are gun mounts on the model, and a component with a shape takes the next mount in the die's order): barrel, twin_barrel, rack, blade (katar-style, every one points forward) or dish (a projector, for equipment that can look like a gun: shield projectors, a buff coil); none for what is applied to the whole machine and shows nowhere (armour panels, vents). Each class is built by tools/lowforge in every maker's metal (art/models/shapes); the validator holds it to that list.

design.fantasy: Two swings a round if the dice agree. Ghouls in threes.
design.notes: Reach melee since 26 September (authored melee is allowed now): the front rank, and the back only once the front is gone. 10 October (Ryan): Close removed, so its reach is direct and melee is its tag; its number comes down to direct's band in the stock pass. 11 October (Ryan): the hopper, the Badger's two locked weapons working together: each foe the claw's blows reach puts a load in the Badger's hopper, so its spread turns a crowd into ammunition for the Bullion Fragmenter.

design.fantasy: As many missiles as it could carry. The box on the Badger's deck.
design.niche: Minerva's indirect fire: the tank that reaches the back rank.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 26 September, so the Badger's missiles exist as a component. Renamed from the Missile Rack 9 October (Ryan, the name audit: the old name was bland; Claude proposed the Shotfirer, the mine's blasting man, for Minerva's mining roots, and Ryan made it the Shotfire Rack).

entries.name: Bullion Fragmenter
entries.codex: A sawed-off cannon fed from a crusher hopper.

design.fantasy: One big round. Warm barrel.
design.notes: 6 October (Ryan): the Slug Cannon converted to melee, renamed the Bullion Fragmenter, and locked to the Badger as a funny mining reference; its line kinetic numbers kept (30 to 60, crit 15, 10 heat) as placeholders. Ryan, later 6 October: a sawed-off cannon, not a breaker; melee is very short range, not contact (a shotgun is melee), and the irony is that bullion is so useless it is better crushed and fired. Codex cut 6 October (Ryan: never explain the joke; keep a component's line short). 10 October (Ryan): Close removed, so its reach is direct and melee is its tag; its number comes down to direct's band in the stock pass. 11 October (Ryan): flat 20, and it fires the hopper the Chainsaw Claw fills, +5 a load and at most three a shot, so a full hopper feeds several big shots rather than one burst (Ryan's cap); numbers placeholders.

entries.name: Slugthrower
entries.codex: Minerva's standard gun. It throws a slug.

design.fantasy: The basic Minervan line weapon: a play on flamethrower under Minerva's trope that things have to physically hit other things.
design.niche: The default kinetic gun of the Minervan kit, the Slug Cannon's old numbers (30 to 60, crit 15, 10 heat), on the Armadillo and twice on the Wild Boar.
design.notes: Named by Ryan 6 October over Claude's Iron-Billet Thrower, Ingot Hurler and Billet Launcher: a default weapon wants the plain word. Fills the line-fire hole the Bullion Fragmenter left when it became the Badger's fixed melee piece. Numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: Reliable, unremarkable, always there.
A beam that goes through the wall and the thing hiding behind it.
design.notes: Renamed from the Lance 9 October (Ryan, the name audit): the Lance shared its word with the Photosphere Lance, and a lance is the Arsenal's medieval register anyway; an enfilade is fire along a line of troops, which is what penetrate does.

design.fantasy: Small, rude, lands behind the front rank.
design.notes: Renamed from the Pocket Mortar 9 October (Ryan, the name audit): pocket was also the Baboon's Pocket Paradox; the knee mortar's reference, extra stupid (Ryan).

design.fantasy: Fins. Lots of fins.
design.notes: Renamed from the Heat Sink 9 October (Ryan, the name audit: the old name was bland; Claude proposed the Water Jacket, the old machine gun's cooling sleeve, and Ryan made it the Coolant Jacket). It shares Coolant with W&S's Coolant Dump.

design.fantasy: The back rank's problem, twice per die.
Lands, then keeps landing.
Whatever it was about to do, it is not doing it now.
design.notes: Renamed from the Shock Barrage 9 October (Ryan, the name audit): Shock is a keyword and a status since the content revision, and this one suppresses.

design.fantasy: Empties the reactor jacket onto the ground. Or onto a friend.
Kestrel removed the safety interlock and called it a feature.
design.notes: Was overcharge (double damage, double heat) at 50 and 20; the keyword is retired and the numbers baked in (26 September). A temporary component either way.

design.fantasy: For finishing what someone else started.
design.niche: The assassin's finisher: flat, and it grows with the target's missing hull, so the face shows what it will deal to the foe it is held over.
design.notes: 10 October (Ryan, bible section 5): Execute retired; flat, +5 for every 20 hull the target is missing (placeholders). To be locked on the Sparrowhawk with a subtler bird name, the Coriolis Accelerator kept for another component; locked in the stock pass, where the Goshawk's hardpoint takes a basic. Its sound stays the gun's (a flat barrel would derive the laser). 11 October (Ryan): named the Pinion Driver (a wing's flight feathers, and a gear; never a rifle, since a locked Kestrel piece would not be called one); the id with it.

design.fantasy: Lightning that picks its own second target.
design.notes: Renamed from the Arc Projector 6 October (Ryan: makes sense and also no sense).

design.fantasy: A very expensive bubble.
design.notes: Renamed from the Deflector 9 October (Ryan, the name audit: the old name was bland; laminar is the smooth-airflow word, Kestrel's aerodynamics register). 12 October (Ryan): the twist, so a Kestrel shield that is not a basic carries Kestrel's own keyword: 20 with rapid (a plain 30 before), shield, roll again and act. 20 October (Ryan): a Rapid shield is never below tier two (a Rapid vent never below tier three), so with the stock pass it leaves the tier-one and tier-two stocks that carry it today and becomes a tier-two blueprint, found; its Rapid stays.

design.fantasy: A shadow falls across the target and it forgets what it was about to do.
design.niche: Aphelion's suppress: a flat energy number on a line, so the control lands every time it comes up.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 26 September; name and numbers are Ryan's to move. Renamed from the Umbra Projector 6 October (Ryan: more slick).

design.fantasy: Lobbed light. It lands at the same brightness every time and keeps burning.
design.niche: Indirect burn at a flat number: predictable stacks for the passive to read.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 26 September. 10 October (Ryan, bible section 5): Steady retired, so it is a flat 10 (it was 5 to 15 steady).

design.fantasy: A ring of light that scours whatever the rift left on the metal.
design.niche: The cleanse carrier: shield an ally and clear its statuses. A unique unlock, not Aphelion stock (28 September).
design.notes: Claude's fill, 26 September.

design.fantasy: A small fast gun that gives the machine its turn back.
design.niche: The tempo tool: a rapid entry so a control frame gets another look at its die.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 26 September; the first rapid component in the pool. Stocked on no chassis since 9 October (the content revision: the Baboon's two became the Probe and the Projector, the Stingray's the Halo Shield), so it carries its own tier, one, as when the Baboon stocked it. Tier two since the same day (Ryan: it carries Rapid, so it reads as a tier-two weapon). Renamed from the Pulse Repeater the same day (Ryan, the name audit): the Flakshot Repeater had the word first, and a vacillating pulse is the rapid entry's back-and-forth.

design.fantasy: The Armadillo's weapon ports seal and the shell goes dark. Everything shoots the shell, because the shell is the only thing there is.
design.niche: The Armadillo's locked shield: while the shutters stand Faraday Hull answers blows on the shield as well as on hull.
design.notes: Sealed Live is shock_on_block, which holds while the component is not destroyed. Was the Faraday Shutters (Claude's fill, 28 September); renamed and re-cut on Ryan's note of 30 September: locking the ports does not electrocute anything, it locks the ports. Carried the taunt keyword from 30 September to 2 October, when taunt went (the bible's targeting row in section 5): the shutters keep the shield and the passive and lose the draw; a lure of the Armadillo's own, if it wants one, is a weapon's to carry.

passive.name: Sealed Live
passive.description: While the shutters stand, Faraday Hull applies to blows on the shield as well.

design.fantasy: A siren and a strobe on a plate of armour. Everything in earshot comes for it.
design.niche: The accessible lure (Ryan, 28 September: damage redirection should be common, not locked; 2 October: a lure rides on a foe-targeted entry, and this one does nothing else).
design.notes: A lure with a spread since 2 October: an indirect entry of no damage that turns the foe it is aimed at and its neighbours on the Badger for the round. Was a shield with the taunt keyword (30 September to 2 October). In the Honey Badger's stock since 30 September (Ryan: the starter set needs class-based mitigation so tanks can protect their team; an intercept is the other candidate, unwritten). Its shape is a dish for want of a siren class.

design.fantasy: The Wild Boar's front end: a ram and a plow blade that go through a wall or a rank of fodder at the same speed.
design.niche: The Boar's locked melee: one big cleaving hit that braces the Boar behind its blade.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September. 10 October (Ryan): Close removed, so its reach is direct and melee is its tag; its number comes down to direct's band in the stock pass. 12 October (Ryan: "Give the plow braced. It fits."): spending it Braces the Boar until the round's end (two stacks, a placeholder), in place of the Glacis, a flat armour +5 that was meant for front-rank blows only and measured no different that way (11 October), so it was hidden base armour.

design.fantasy: A drum-fed scattergun on a pintle, its shells bursting into a rank of foes. Fire, and the car is already moving. Ryan, 19 October: "a low damage, spread, maybe rapid, weapon with a new debuff: flak".
design.niche: The Prairie Dog's locked gun and the maker's first Flak piece: a flat 5 that sprays the target's rank (Spread), rolls again (Rapid) and lays Flak 2 on each foe hit, so the team's many small blows land harder. The softener's round: spray, roll again, cash.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list. Ryan's go, 19 October (the bible's Prairie Dog row; the brief retired to git: git show f5a085a:docs/briefs/ws_prairie_dog.md): Direct, flat 5 (5 to 15 rolled before), Spread, Rapid, Flak 2, heat 0, every number a placeholder. The Spread and the flat 5 are built; Flak is a planned keyword the die builds the entry without until the engine has the numbered keyword and the halving status (the to-do), so the gun sprays today and lays nothing. The flak field on the face is the keyword's number, to align with the numbers branch's numbered-keyword field when it merges. Three keywords is the authored cap, carried by a tier-one locked piece because its number is the lowest in the game.

design.fantasy: A barbed dart on a cable and a capacitor the size of the car. Whatever it pins takes the next blow double.
design.niche: The Dingo's locked support: a cheap Shock on the foe an ally is about to eat, so the ally's blow lands double.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list. 14 October (Ryan, the go on the roster analysis): Shock in place of Suppress, the first locked piece that amplifies for others, and the only hard control on a tier-one chassis gone (docs/briefs/ws_dingo.md).

design.fantasy: The Goshawk's engines fire forward for one shot. The hotter the airframe, the bigger the shot, and the airframe is cold afterwards.
design.niche: The Goshawk's burst: spend the heat the passive was living on.
design.notes: Live since the engine reads vents_all and power_per_heat (30 September). Claude's fill, 28 September. Needs a face that vents all heat as it fires and adds power per 10 heat vented (vents_all and power_per_heat below); planned until the engine reads them.

design.fantasy: Fists, and a temper: every hit the Nemesis takes, its own included, is another swing it gets to throw.
design.niche: The Nemesis's locked melee and its rage's outlet: spent with rage banked, it spends one and the die rolls again, and nothing switches off, so a long rage chains the fists.
design.notes: 12 October (Ryan): the Nemesis gets new fists that spend rage to roll the die again ("you just get rapid", without the switch-off, since rage is the limit), and the Gravity Knuckles go to tier three. The name is Ryan's working name, a Bruce Lee reference (Fist of Fury), open. The Gravity Knuckles' numbers are carried over (15 flat, 10 heat). 13 October (Ryan): the name stays, and no Burn: "it has no place".

design.fantasy: Fists that weigh what the Arsenal says they weigh. Each blow burns, and each blow costs the machine a little of itself.
design.niche: The Nemesis's locked melee: energy, static, burning, and volatile so every punch feeds the Crucible.
design.notes: Live since volatile landed (30 September). Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list. Planned until volatile exists. 10 October (Ryan): Close removed, so its reach is direct and melee is its tag; its number comes down to direct's band in the stock pass. 10 October (Ryan): volatile off; with the Nemesis's passive reading hull damage, a self-biting fist was a ramp and a payoff in one, so no other entry was ever worth spending. Something more like gravity is open (half damage to the foes beside it, or pulling a back-rank foe forward). 12 October (Ryan): off the Nemesis, which gets new fists that spend rage (the Knuckle of Fury); the Gravity Knuckles become a tier-three blueprint with the effect measured on 11 October (volatile back and an area keyword in place of Burn), the tier three keeping the word gravity and the Nemesis the word knuckles, so its second word is open. Its entry is unchanged until the name and the area keywords land. 13 October (Ryan): the gravity idea is shelved, with lots of potential; it comes back later.

design.fantasy: Four blades that take something from what they kill. The Arsenal's manual calls it attunement.
design.niche: The Ammit's locked melee: flat, and devour to grow; the machine's scaling threat for the whole battle and nothing more.
design.notes: Live since devour landed (30 September). Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list. Planned until devour and Overcharged exist. 10 October (Ryan, bible section 5): Execute dropped (it was probably too strong with it anyway); no heal suppression or utility here, any of that on a stock tier two or three component of the Ammit's. 10 October (Ryan): Close removed, so its reach is direct and melee is its tag; its number comes down to direct's band in the stock pass. 11 October (Ryan): devour folded into a rule printed on the talons, its one carrier, so it is no longer a keyword to learn.

design.fantasy: Mining kit with the safety plate off. It puts a rivet through anything.
design.niche: Minerva's starter gun.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September: the maker starter kits.

design.fantasy: A chimney that opens. Minerva's answer to heat is a bigger pipe.
design.niche: Minerva's starter vent.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September.

design.fantasy: The gun every Kestrel airframe leaves the factory with. Light, flat, warm.
design.niche: Kestrel's starter gun.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list.

design.fantasy: An intake that opens to the slipstream. Cooling by going fast.
design.niche: Kestrel's starter vent.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September.

design.fantasy: A plain coherent beam, the one Aphelion gun that does exactly what it says.
design.niche: Aphelion's generic line weapon: a flat number, no keyword.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September, so Aphelion's stock has a plain gun.

design.fantasy: A ring of hard light. Nothing clever about it, which Aphelion resents.
design.niche: Aphelion's generic shield.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September; the Corona Shield with cleanse is the unique one. Stocked on the Stingray since 9 October (the content revision), in place of its Pulse Vacillator, so its tier is derived (two).

design.fantasy: Kestrel's answer to a regulator: a coil that pushes an ally's guns past the line for one round.
design.niche: The first buff component: two stacks of Overcharged on a machine for the round.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 29 September, so the buff kind has one entry in the pool; fitted to no chassis. Numbers, name and maker are Ryan's to move.

design.fantasy: A deep-space radiator, unfolded. Heat goes where it always went: out.
design.niche: Aphelion's starter vent, so the Mandrill need not borrow one.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September.

design.fantasy: The Arsenal's issue weapon, older than it looks: plasma loaded like powder, and no two shots alike.
design.niche: The Arsenal's starter gun.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September. Renamed from the Plasma Carbine 9 October (Ryan, the name audit): carbine is W&S's word and the Laser Carbine already carries it; an arquebus is the Arsenal's medieval firearm. 10 October (Ryan, bible section 5): By its niche it rolls (an old, unreliable gun), 5 to 15 for the flat 10 it was; the sound stays plasma (a rolled barrel would derive gunfire).

design.fantasy: A stream of plasma that sticks. Purification, the manual says.
design.niche: The Arsenal's starter burn.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list.

design.fantasy: Plasma lobbed high and falling burning.
design.niche: The Arsenal's advanced piece, pre-installed on the Nemesis: indirect burn that runs hot.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list.

design.fantasy: Heat condensed and thrown away. Nobody outside the Arsenal knows where.
design.niche: The Arsenal's vent: the biggest number, paid in hull, and on the Nemesis every vent is a Crucible stack.
design.notes: Claude's fill, 28 September; the name is from Ryan's list. 12 October (Ryan): the twist, so the Arsenal's equipment is its biggest number paid in hull like the Oblation Mantle: 40 with volatile (a plain 30 before).

design.fantasy: A beam drawn off the reactor's own surface. It burns what it touches and the machine with it.
design.niche: The Stingray's locked gun: a hot energy burn on a line, so the passive always has heat to read and a stack to deepen.
design.notes: Proposed and decided 2 October (the Stingray row of the bible). Numbers are placeholders, Ryan's to move.

design.fantasy: A lattice of light laid over a machine's weapons. Everything it hits afterwards keeps burning.
design.niche: Aphelion's buff: a stack of Primed for the round, on itself or an ally, so the Stingray's suite has a buff to deepen as well as its burns.
design.notes: Proposed and decided 2 October. The second buff component in the pool after Kestrel's Overcharge Coil; numbers are Ryan's to move.

entries.name: Backwash Ionizer
entries.codex: Ionizes the target's backwash, temporarily increasing the target's shield capacity until round end.

design.fantasy: The whole front of the Puffin is one shield projector, and it only points outward.
design.niche: The Puffin's locked shield: a big bubble it can only raise on an ally, and the game's first Overshield, so it may lift the ally past its maximum for the round (Ryan, 2 October: a shield specialist, not a shield-bot; 5 October: overshield a rare keyword, the projector first).
design.notes: Proposed 2 October. Decided 5 October with the Puffin's passive: the projector carries Overshield, the passive vents the ally it shields. Overshield's excess fades at the round's end; it is never on the Puffin itself, since the projector is fixed and allies-only. Numbers are placeholders. Renamed from the Prow Projector 6 October (Ryan: janky; a shield that grants extra shield by ionizing the target's backwash, whatever that means, is the house joke done right).

design.fantasy: A probe lobbed into the formation. Whatever the thing it lands beside was about to do, it now differentiates.
design.niche: The first Disrupt in the pool: an indirect entry of no damage that turns a foe onto its other move. It deals nothing, so it counts for Aphelion's Sponsorship.
design.notes: Stocked on the Baboon in place of a Pulse Vacillator. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: Whatever the rift left on the metal goes straight from solid to gone, with the heat.
design.niche: Aphelion's cleanse vent: the Chorus's answer in a stock kit, where the Corona Shield is a unique unlock.
design.notes: Stocked on the Baboon in place of the Radiator Sail, so it is Aphelion's tier-one vent. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders. Renamed from the Sublimation Array the same day (Ryan, the name audit: a Sublimator, with an adjective; he chose Phased).

design.fantasy: It projects polarity. Nobody at Aphelion will say what that means, and the next thing to hit the target hits twice as hard.
design.niche: The first Shock: a line entry of no damage that sets up a doubled blow for the team. Shocked is a status, so it feeds the Baboon's Pocket Paradox, which a suppress never does.
design.notes: Ryan's own example of the house joke (bible, the component-names row of 6 October). Stocked on the Baboon in place of its second Pulse Vacillator. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: A hydraulic pit prop jammed under a machine's plating. It holds the roof up in the mine; it holds the armour on out here.
design.niche: The first Braced carrier: armour +20 for the round on itself or an ally, the answer to volume (swarms, double strikes, a storm of small blows), nothing against a breach.
design.notes: Stocked on the Armadillo in place of its Ablative Plating. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: A slab of mine-shaft door on a hydraulic arm, swung across in front of whoever needs it.
design.niche: Minerva's hardpoint shield: a slab on an arm, raised on itself or an ally. The platings left the dice for modules on 9 October, so a shield on a hardpoint wants to be something mounted.
design.notes: Built 9 October in the content revision as Minerva's intercept, with the Guard keyword (allies only, the foes aimed at the ally turning on the spender, its shield going up on the door); Guard taken out the same day (Ryan: until we feel we need it), so it is a plain shield, self or ally. On the Wild Boar and the Clydesdale in place of their Ablative Plating.

design.fantasy: Mining gauntlets with the arc welder left switched on. What they punch stays live.
design.niche: Melee that Shocks what it hits and leaves standing: the Armadillo's status on a weapon (Ryan's board), so the next blow on it lands double.
design.notes: From Ryan's Names board. Stocked on no chassis, so it carries its own tier. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders. Halved to 10 to 20 when the branch met the damage scale (9 October; bible section 11, the damage-scale row). 10 October (Ryan, bible section 5): By its niche it is flat (a shock rider), 15 for the 10 to 20 it was. 10 October (Ryan): Close removed, so its reach is direct and melee is its tag; its number comes down to direct's band in the stock pass.

design.fantasy: A ward projected from the machine's own reactor, paid for out of its frame. The manual calls it devotion.
design.niche: The biggest shield in the pool, paid in the spender's hull: raised on an ally, the Arsenal machine bleeds to cover a friend.
design.notes: Stocked on the Ammit in place of its Ward Plate. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders. A projector since 9 October (Ryan: plating belongs in modules, a hardpoint carries something mounted), its shape a dish and its fantasy no longer plating. On the Nemesis in place of its Ward Plate as well. 15 October (Ryan): renamed the Oblation Mantle from the Oblation Ward, Ward being the buff's word (the bible's Barrier and Ward row); the id stays, as the Bone Wyvern's did.

design.fantasy: A censer swung over the hull. Whatever strikes the consecrated metal is marked for what comes next.
design.niche: The first Retaliate carrier: for two rounds, a foe that strikes the machine's bare hull is Shocked, so the Armadillo's Faraday Hull can ride on any machine; on the Nemesis its own punches spend the shocks.
design.notes: Stocked on the Nemesis in place of its Plasma Carbine. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: A minigun, but more. Three bursts a pull, each rolled on its own.
design.niche: The first multi-strike: three small blows that each roll, crit and proc on their own. Strong into bare foes and with Primed, almost useless into armour 10.
design.notes: From Ryan's Names board (the horde gun). Stocked on the Clydesdale in place of one Twin Autoguns. Decided 9 October in the content revision (more support and status entries everywhere, Aphelion's most; Ryan: the names in the right register). Numbers are placeholders. At the damage scale (9 October) its strikes are 5 to 10, half of 5 to 15 rounded up to fives as the scale rounds (a kinetic weapon rolls a range): 22 or so a spend against the Twin Autoguns' 10, a little hotter than the old ratio, and about 7 into armour 5, which is its weakness (bible section 11, the damage-scale row).

design.fantasy: A diffuser on the exhaust that spreads the wake thin. It runs cooler, and somehow faster.
design.niche: A combined entry: a vent of 10 that also shields 10, so a support entry is never a dead roll and costs its turn like any other.
design.notes: From Ryan's Names board. Stocked on the Puffin in place of its Ram-air Scoop. Decided 9 October in the content revision as the first Rapid equipment (the escort cools an ally and acts again). Ryan, 20 October: Rapid off, a vent that shields in its place (vent 10, shield 10), the action-economy row's cantrip by density; Rapid vents and shields, if any exist, never below tier three. The vent half runs today; the shield half (a shields field on the face) lands with the combined entry's engine (the to-do), on the Puffin's passive a vent twice. Numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: A canister of wire and resin lobbed at a foe's feet (Ryan's working name). It bursts after the foe has moved, and the foe beside it is caught in the same net.
design.niche: The funnel-web's locked control, kept as hard control under the stun row (Ryan, 17 October: it fits the kit): a delayed Suppress on the webbed foe (its next action) and the next foe to act beside it (this one), no damage, no cooldown. Web the foe left of the threat for safety now; web the boss to open a window on it next round.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 18 October (the bible's funnel-web row; the brief retired to git, bfa8cf2). The web keyword is planned, so the die builds this entry without it until the engine has it. Numbers are placeholders and the name a working one. Lands on the foe as Webbed, the chip carrying the burst's timer (the to-do).

design.fantasy: The cylinder's motor. Ryan, 18 October: "spin the barrel, rapid, no cooldown, next component gets +5 damage or something"; the drum spins up and the next shot leaves hotter, a minigun's spin-up inside a revolver's cylinder.
design.niche: The Cassowary's locked combo piece: no damage, Rapid with no cooldown, no heat and no Volatile, its reroll a true spin of the cylinder over every chamber, itself included; each spin grants a stack of Spun Up (+5 on the next weapon spend, carried between turns). Its limiter is the cylinder: a stepping die cannot chain it into itself, and the way back to it in a round runs through the other chambers' switch-offs or the team's rerolls. The chase: spin into a Rapid piece into the Spin-Up into the big gun.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 19 October (the bible's Cassowary row; the brief retired to git: git show 021f075:docs/briefs/ws_revolver.md). The names are his (Spin-Up, Spun Up).
